stem:
Ovi needs to separate fine rice flour from larger husk pieces using a kitchen sieve.

Which choice is correct?

options.text: Use holes between the sizes of the husk and the fine flour so husk stays on top and flour passes through.
Use holes larger than both the husk and the flour; both will still separate cleanly.
With holes between their sizes, the fine flour stays on the sieve and the bigger husk falls through.
Sieving will also remove dissolved salt from salty water poured through the same sieve.

teacher.key_rationale: Sieving separates solids by size when holes sit between the particle sizes: larger husk stays; finer flour passes. Holes larger than both fail; dissolved salt is not separated by sieving.
